Configuration files and environment variables

The files SATOM reads its configuration from — /opt/satom/.env and the environment variables it honours, the ACME provider catalog, the documentation redaction overlay and the HA node list — with meanings and defaults.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereServer side — /opt/satom/.env, /opt/satom/acme_providers.yaml, /opt/satom/data/

Overview#

Almost everything an operator tunes in SATOM is stored in the database and edited in the UI (Settings). A small set of values has to exist before the application can reach its database, and those live in files on the node:

File Purpose Edited by
/opt/satom/.env Secrets, database URL, run mode, optional overrides Installer; by hand for overrides
/opt/satom/acme_providers.yaml Seed catalog of ACME DNS-01 providers Shipped with the release
/opt/satom/data/publication-rules.local.json Site-specific redaction rules for published documentation Operator
/opt/satom/data/ha_nodes.json The HA node list (names, addresses, roles) Installer and High Availability → HA nodes
/opt/satom/deploy/metrics-store.env Pinned version and checksum of the metrics-store binary Shipped with the release

The .env file#

The installer writes /opt/satom/.env once:

SECRET_KEY=<random>
FERNET_KEY=<random Fernet key>
SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI=postgresql+psycopg://satom:<password>@127.0.0.1/satom
FLASK_ENV=production
NODE_IP=192.0.2.10
WEB_PORT=443
  • Owner root, group = service account, mode 0640. The application and the timers read it; nothing in the application writes it.
  • systemd loads it with EnvironmentFile= for every unit; wsgi.py additionally loads the .env that sits next to it (without overriding values systemd already set), so manual runs from another directory still see it.
  • systemd reads EnvironmentFile only when a unit starts. Restart satom.service and satom-scheduler.service after editing .env.

⚠️Warning — Never regenerate FERNET_KEY

FERNET_KEY decrypts every stored appliance password and secret. If it is lost or replaced, those credentials cannot be recovered. The installer refuses to reinstall over an active node unless SATOM_ALLOW_REINSTALL=1 is set, because a reinstall writes a new .env. See Security model.

Environment variables#

Only variables the code actually reads are listed. "—" means unset by default.

Core#

Variable Meaning Default Read in
FLASK_ENV production selects the production configuration; anything else selects development (debug on, insecure cookies) development app/config.py
SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI Database URL. Required in production — the app refuses to start without it rather than fall back to SQLite dev/test fallback: a SQLite file app/config.py
SECRET_KEY Signs sessions, CSRF tokens and password-reset links random per process if unset (sessions then break on restart) app/config.py
FERNET_KEY Encrypts stored credentials none — start-up fails without it outside tests app/config.py, app/services/encryption.py
MAX_UPLOAD_MB Maximum request body, in MB (larger uploads get 413) 600 app/config.py
PORT Port for python wsgi.py development runs only 8000 wsgi.py

Network and security#

Variable Meaning Default Read in
TRUSTED_PROXIES Comma-separated proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted for rate limiting and audit 127.0.0.1,::1 app/extensions.py
LINK_HOSTS Comma-separated extra host names that absolute links mailed out of a request (the password-reset link) may use. The node's own host name and FQDN are always accepted; a request arriving under any other Host gets a link to the node FQDN instead. Not Flask's TRUSTED_HOSTS: every Host is still served, so by-IP health and peer probes keep working — app/config.py, app/auth/routes.py
RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI Flask-Limiter storage. redis://… shares limits across workers memory:// app/config.py
CACHE_REDIS_URI Redis for the shared JSON cache; if unset, RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI is used when it is a redis:// URL — (in-process cache) app/services/cache.py
SATOM_PEER_TLS_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED Emergency override for HA pairs: 1 lets a peer request whose certificate does not verify retry encrypted but unverified (with a logged warning) instead of being refused. Remove it once the node certificate is fixed off app/services/node_security.py
FORTINET_HOST_CONCURRENCY Maximum concurrent API requests per appliance 4 app/clients/base.py
FORTINET_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_KEY Allow a temporary FERNET_KEY for throwaway runs. Never in production — app/services/encryption.py

ℹ️Note — When to set LINK_HOSTS

Set it when users reach the node under a name that is not its own — a public alias or a reverse proxy in front of it — so the password-reset email links to that name rather than to the node FQDN, which they may not be able to reach:

LINK_HOSTS=satom.example.com,console.example.com

Names are compared case-insensitively and without the port; a kept link also keeps the port it came in on. The value is read when the service starts, so restart satom.service after changing it. Leave it unset when users open the node by its own name.

ℹ️Note — Rate-limit storage on host installs

The host installer does not set RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI, so each gunicorn worker keeps its own counters. The container stack sets it to its Redis service. Add RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0 to .env if a local Redis is available.

First start#

Variable Meaning Default Read in
SATOM_ADMIN_PASSWORD Password for the first admin account, used only when the users table is empty — (a random password is generated) app/__init__.py
SATOM_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE Where the generated password is written (mode 0600) /opt/satom/initial-admin-password app/__init__.py
FORTINET_SKIP_DB_BOOTSTRAP Skip table creation and seeding at start-up (for migration tooling) — app/__init__.py

Metrics, jobs and updates#

Variable Meaning Default Read in
SATOM_METRICS_URL Metrics store URL. Ranked below the metrics.vm_url setting, above the built-in default http://127.0.0.1:8428 app/services/vm_store.py
SATOM_DEVICE_JOBS 0/false/off/no disables running device actions as jobs 1 app/services/device_jobs.py
SATOM_JOB_INLINE_S Seconds a request waits for its job before answering with a job reference 2.0 app/services/device_jobs.py
SATOM_DEVICE_LOCK_MAX_WAIT_S How long a queued write waits for another job's device lock 1800 app/services/job_progress.py
FM_UPDATE_BRANCH Git branch the self-update follows main app/services/self_update.py
FM_NODE_NAME Node name shown in HA and update views host name app/services/self_update.py
FM_HEALTH_URL / FM_HEALTH_TIMEOUT Health check used by the update runner after a restart http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz / 90 s deploy/self_update_runner.py
FM_APP_USER Service account for the update runner owner of /opt/satom deploy/self_update_runner.py
SATOM_API_PACK_AUTO 0 stops the update runner importing the shipped API library pack 1 deploy/self_update_runner.py
SATOM_TRUST_DIR Directory of public keys trusted for update packages /etc/satom/update-keys app/services/update_package_service.py
SATOM_PACK_KEY_DIR Root of the operator-added pack keys, one sub-directory per lane (api_pack, knowledge); the release's own keys ship in deploy/pack-keys/ /etc/satom/pack-keys app/services/api_pack.py
SATOM_UPGRADE_FEED Release feed URL (for a mirror or fork) the project's public feed deploy/upgrade_feed.py

Storage locations#

These exist mainly for tests and unusual layouts; leave them unset on a normal node. Defaults are relative to /opt/satom.

Variable Default
FM_APP_DIR /opt/satom
FORTINET_REPORTS_DIR data/reports
SATOM_SOT_DIR data/sot
SATOM_BACKUPS_DIR data/system_backups
SATOM_VAULT_DIR data/backups (configuration-backup vault)
SATOM_JOBS_DIR data/jobs
SATOM_REDISCOVERY_DIR data/rediscovery
SATOM_ARTIFACT_DIR data/artifacts
SATOM_API_MATRIX_DIR data/api_matrix
SATOM_CERT_ARCHIVE_DIR data/cert-renew-archive
FORTINET_DIAG_DIR data/diagnostics
FM_DATA_DIR data (pre/post-flight baselines go to data/flight/)
SATOM_STATE_DIR /opt/satom/state

The trust store for appliance CAs is pki/trust under the application directory unless SATOM_TRUST_DIR is set — the same variable that relocates the update-package keys.

Installer inputs#

installers/install-satom.sh reads, among others, SATOM_APP_USER (service-account name, default satom), SATOM_SERVED_NAMES (host names the node answers to — used for the certificate and the nginx server_name) and SATOM_ALLOW_REINSTALL. See Installation.

Container deployments#

SATOM_RUNTIME and SATOM_AGENT tell the application it runs in the container stack (which changes how services are controlled). They are set by the compose files, not by hand.

ACME provider catalog#

/opt/satom/acme_providers.yaml lists the DNS-01 providers offered by the certificate manager: for each one a slug, label, the ACME client flag (lego --dns <flag>), a documentation link and the environment variables the provider needs (secret: true fields are Fernet-encrypted and never sent back to the browser).

  • The file is an insert-only seed: at start-up rows missing from the acme_dns_providers table are added; existing rows are never overwritten. After that the table belongs to the operator; the provider is chosen in Settings → Certificate Manager (ACME, DNS provider).
  • The file is generated by deploy/gen_acme_providers.py from the installed ACME client. acme_providers.overlay.yaml holds hand-made corrections the generator merges in: a deny list (for example the interactive manual provider) and extend entries that add or override fields. The overlay is not read at run time.

See Certificates.

Documentation redaction overlay#

data/publication-rules.local.json holds the site-specific rules used to redact internal names and addresses before documentation is published (redactions, plus a forbidden list the output is re-scanned against). Generic rules (address ranges, personal e-mail) are built in.

  • It lives in data/ so the HA data sync and backup bundles carry it; a copy in the application root is still read as a fallback.
  • On a deployed node (one with a .env), a missing or malformed file is an error rather than "no rules", so redaction can never silently fail open.

HA node list#

data/ha_nodes.json is a JSON list of {name, host, role} entries. The installer writes it; --authorize-peer on the primary adds the standby; it is edited under High Availability → HA nodes; the data sync reads it to find its peer. The installer never overwrites an entry that already exists. Because data/ is replicated from the primary with --delete, the primary's copy is authoritative. See High availability.

Advanced Configuration classes

app/config.py defines Config, DevelopmentConfig and ProductionConfig. Shared settings: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True, SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE="Lax", WTF_CSRF_TIME_LIMIT=3600, SQLAlchemy pool_pre_ping=True and pool_recycle=1800. Development turns DEBUG on and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE off. Production sets SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT=86400 so static files are cacheable for a day.

Advanced Leftover files

Older trees may contain endpoints*.yaml files (for example endpoints.yaml.pre-… backups). The endpoint registry no longer reads YAML: it is seeded from the JSON baselines in app/registry/baselines/. See API registry.

#.env#environment#variables#config#secret_key#fernet_key#database uri#flask_env#trusted_proxies#link_hosts#ratelimit#redis#acme#publication rules#ha_nodes.json
